title: test-bm configuration
description: Per-bookmarklet test configuration for test-bm.js. Each key is a bookmarklet name, which is the file name in JSFormatted without its .js. A bookmarklet with no entry gets the default safe run: example.com, one run, a settle period, and a pass when it parsed, ran and threw nothing.

$schema.description: Points at this file, so an editor offers completion and validation.

entry.description: What a run does with one bookmarklet.

url.description: The page to open. Defaults to https://example.com/, which is reserved for documentation. A url of the form fixture:<file>.html is a page in test/fixtures/pages, served from https://fixtures.test/ without a network: a real origin, so localStorage, the clipboard and location behave as they do on a site. A hash may follow the file name. A fixture naming a page that is not there is a configuration error. A url of the form $NAME names an environment variable holding the address, for a page whose address does not belong in the repository: the address is read when the entry runs and never written down, every reason and report naming the variable in its place, and an unset variable is a skip rather than a failure.

capture.description: Write a screenshot of the page either side of the bookmarklet, and a video of the whole entry, into test-results/test-bm/<run>/capture/<name>/. Each artifact's path and the offset into the video at which every step started go in the report, so a clip can be cut to the moment the bookmarklet ran. --capture does the same for every entry a run reaches. A failure keeps failure.png whether or not the entry asked to be captured. An entry with auth captures nothing and refuses this, because a signed-in page shows the account and what it holds.

scheduled.description: Include this entry in node test-bm.js --scheduled. Only for pages that load headless with no consent wall and no bot check.

requires.description: The CSS selectors the bookmarklet reads, taken from its source rather than from memory. Each is checked before the bookmarklet runs, and a missing one fails with "site changed: <selector> not found on <url>".

steps.description: What to do on the page, in order. The bookmarklet runs once: at the step that names it, or after load when no step does.

dialogs.description: Answers to alert, confirm and prompt, in the order they appear. A dialog with no answer left is dismissed.

permissions.description: Browser permissions the context grants, such as clipboard-read and clipboard-write. An expect on a clipboard value needs clipboard-read.

skip.description: A reason to list the entry as skipped without running it. A skip never fails a run.
examples: the page serves a consent wall to a headless browser

timeout.description: Milliseconds the whole entry is allowed, after which it fails.

settle.description: Milliseconds to wait after the last step, for anything the bookmarklet started.

auth.description: The sign-in this entry needs, by site name. test-bm.js never signs in itself: it asks the launcher module named by TEST_BM_AUTH_LAUNCHER, an absolute path outside the repository, for a signed-in browser context. Without one the entry is a skip. An entry with auth runs read-only, writes down nothing the page shows, names signedIn, and is never scheduled. Entries that share a sign-in share the name.

network.description: The hosts other than the page's own that the bookmarklet may send a request to, each with the reason. A request the bookmarklet makes to any other host fails the entry, because a bookmarklet sends nothing from the page anywhere else. A site's own API on another host, or a library pinned by its integrity hash, is what belongs here.

host.description: An exact host, or *. and a domain for any of its subdomains.

examples: the file sizes come from GitHub's own REST API

signedIn.description: A selector only the signed-in page has, checked before requires. A page without it, or one that lands on another origin, is a skip reading "signed out of <site>" rather than a site-changed failure.

step.description: One thing to do. Exactly one of run, click, fill, press, select, wait or expect.

run.description: Run the bookmarklet here, rather than after load. A second run step runs it again, which is how a bookmarklet that turns itself off on the second run is checked.

fill.description: A selector to type into, with the value beside it or nested in an object.

press.description: A key to press, such as Enter or Control+c. With a selector beside it, the key goes to that element.

select.description: A selector whose text to select, the way a reader drags across it. The range is set inside the element's text node, which is the shape a drag leaves and the shape the bookmarklets that style selected text read.

wait.description: Milliseconds to wait, or a selector to wait for.

selector.description: The element a press goes to.

value.description: The value a fill types, when fill is written as a selector on its own.

text.description: The value a fill types, written the other way round.

expect.description: What should be true. A selector that is visible or hidden, matches a count, matches as many elements as another selector, or holds some text; or a clipboard value; or where the page is; or where a new tab went.

hidden.description: The first match is not showing.

count.description: How many elements the selector matches, exactly.

matches.description: A second selector, whose matches are counted against the first selector's. It is for one thing per row of something the page lists, where the count the page would give changes whenever the page does and the relation does not: a size cell in every file row, say. The failure names both counts.

text.description: Text the first match holds somewhere in it.

clipboard.description: What the clipboard holds, trimmed at both ends. The whole value, not a part of it. Needs clipboard-read in permissions.

location.description: Text the page's address holds somewhere in it, for a bookmarklet that navigates. Chromium keeps a text fragment directive out of the address, so a bookmarklet that writes one is read off the page it moved instead.

popup.description: Text the address of a new tab the bookmarklet opened holds somewhere in it, for a bookmarklet that opens a link in a new tab. Waits for the tab, up to the entry's timeout or ten seconds.

accept.description: Accept it rather than dismissing it.

text.description: What to type into a prompt before accepting it.
